The must-sees

  • Castle Hill

    Viewpoint

    A castle stood here until Louis XIV’s troops demolished it in 1706. Today the hilltop is a park with an artificial waterfall and the city’s classic view.

    Look for: On the hill’s north side, the old castle cemetery holds the grave of Léon Gambetta, a founder of the French Third Republic.

  • Chagall Museum

    Museum · 1973

    It opened in 1973 during Chagall’s lifetime to house his Biblical Message paintings. He also designed the stained glass windows of its concert hall.

    Look for: Outside, a large Chagall mosaic of the prophet Elijah in his fiery chariot is reflected in a shallow pool.

  • Cours Saleya

    Market

    The flower and produce market is held here most mornings, and antiques fill the stalls on Mondays. The low buildings on its seaward side, the Ponchettes, have flat roofs once used as a promenade.

    Look for: At the eastern end, the large yellow building on Place Charles-Félix was Matisse’s home and studio from 1921 to 1938; he painted the sea from its windows.

  • Hôtel Negresco

    Hotel · 1913

    Henri Negresco, a Romanian-born hotelier, opened it in 1913 in a building by Édouard-Jean Niermans. It is now a listed historic monument.

  • Matisse Museum

    Museum

    Henri Matisse lived in Nice from 1917 until his death in 1954. The museum holds works that he and his family left to the city.

    Look for: Beside the villa are the ruins of Roman Cemenelum, including a small amphitheatre among the olive trees.

  • Old Town

    Neighbourhood

    This was the walled town until the 18th century, when Nice began to spread beyond it. Its baroque churches and Italian-style houses recall centuries of rule by the House of Savoy.

    Look for: On Place Rossetti, the cathedral of Sainte-Réparate wears a dome of glazed coloured tiles.

  • Place Masséna

    Square

    It is named after Marshal André Masséna, who was born in Nice, and was laid out in the 19th century over the Paillon river. The seven lit figures above it are by the artist Jaume Plensa.

    Look for: At the seaward end, the Fountain of the Sun has a towering marble Apollo surrounded by bronze planets.

  • Promenade des Anglais

    Waterfront

    In the 1820s English winter residents paid for a path along the shore, which gave the promenade its name. On 14 July 2016 a truck attack here killed 86 people, and they are remembered along the seafront.

    Look for: Near the Negresco, the white Art Deco front of the Palais de la Méditerranée, a 1929 casino, was kept when the building behind it was rebuilt.

  • Russian Orthodox Cathedral

    Church · 1912

    Consecrated in 1912, it was built for the large Russian community that wintered on the Riviera. It is one of the largest Orthodox churches in Western Europe.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Nice and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Nice passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
